data.name: Dayavanti
data.gender_notes: Dayavanti is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Dayavanti is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'daya', which means charity or compassion. The suffix 'vanti' signifies one who embodies this trait. In Hindu mythology, Dayavanti is the name of a queen known for her generosity and kindness. The name Dayavanti carries the meaning “Giving charity, generous” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dayavanti usually hope their child will grow to embody giving charity, generous and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the selfless act of giving and the power of compassion.
data.etymology: Dayavanti belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Giving charity, generous.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dayavanti total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

historical_references.reference: Dayavanti was the queen consort of the great Maharaja Shivaji (1627-1680 CE) of the Maratha Empire in India. She was a brilliant diplomat and is credited with helping Shivaji expand his kingdom significantly.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Dayavanti is derived from Sanskrit, where 'daya' means compassion and 'vanti' means one who bestows. This name is seen on various literature, media and entertainment platforms, including books, movies, and television series, as well as in educational contexts such as history and cultural studies classes.
